summary: First state to criminalise adult restroom use (HB 257, 2024) — not just school facilities — and first to explicitly prohibit LGBTQ flags at government buildings and schools (May 2025, fines up to $500/day). Below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (the record's URL is malformed - dashes instead of slashes in the date segment - and returns a 404 page; the dossier cites the same New York Times report at the corrected path); the underlying New York Times report of 31 January 2024 covers HB 257, the first-in-the-nation statewide bathroom ban applying to transgender adults, not just schoolgirls - the bill number is independently confirmed by MAP's citations PDF.

Guardian report (29 May 2025) on Pride 2025 in the US: on 7 May Utah became the first state to explicitly prohibit flying LGBTQ+ flags at government buildings and schools, with fines of $500 a day; Utah Pride's executive director says the state 'leads the nation in anti-LGBTQ legislation'; similar flag bans were signed in Idaho and Montana, while Salt Lake City issued counter-flags and Boise made the pride flag an official city flag.

tangentialFactors: The flag ban and the 2025 Pride-season sponsor exodus are visibility conflicts affecting LGBT+ presence broadly rather than trans status specifically - but they shape the climate a visibly trans visitor encounters, and enforcement of the $500/day flag fines reaches ordinary institutional spaces.
